statement: Google Cloud backlog rose by more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion in 2Q26, from $462 billion in Q1 2026, with just over half expected to convert to revenue within 24 months.
why: Backlog is contracted future work, so a half-trillion-dollar book that keeps growing is the strongest available evidence that AI compute demand is committed rather than merely forecast.

impact.mechanism: A growing contracted backlog obliges the cloud provider to keep adding compute capacity, which sustains accelerator and data-center purchasing.

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance (Bloomberg wire) — "Google increases capex forecast again after cloud-driven earnings beat"
evidence.excerpt: Google Cloud's backlog increased by more than $50 billion sequentially, reaching $514 billion in the second quarter.

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance (Bloomberg wire) — "Google increases capex forecast again after cloud-driven earnings beat"
evidence.excerpt: the company expects to recognize just over 50% of the total backlog as revenue over the next 24 months.

confidence.basis: Secondary wire coverage of an earnings release; the backlog figure is explicitly attributed to corroborating coverage rather than a fetched filing, so capped at medium.
